decision.summary: The mandatory-final Mac acceptance failed in hung_supervisor, subcase 'unresolved', at test_git_containment.py:2013 (`kernel.identity(probe.supervisor.pid) == probe.supervisor`). The earlier blocker is fixed on these bytes. closed_status and the eight subcases after it passed, and the stdout log shows the closed_status anchor now proves owned-zombie continuity: one status-2 transition row, then two fresh SZOMB=5 rows. The new failure is in the test controller itself. For case 'unresolved', _git_containment.py:321 deliberately changes anchor.bound.micros by one (the fixed F1 fault). containment_probe_parent.py:49 then reports that changed anchor.bound in the 'unresolved' event. Probe.next (test_git_containment.py:1306) overwrites probe.supervisor from any row carrying 'supervisor', so the probe's record of the supervisor now holds the fault-injected identity instead of the real one from READY/TERMINAL. The fresh kernel identity therefore can't match. Production F1 behaved as specified: primary timeout, state-unknown, handlers and ownership retained. Controller cleanup recorded RESOLVED with a host-only SIGKILL, decision before reap, and absence of the host, supervisor, group and members. owned_processes is []. This is a reproducible, blocking test bug in an allowlisted test file. Note that the original_owned_processes inventory also records the falsified supervisor micros, which the same repair corrects. The remaining hung_supervisor subcases (fixture_failure_*, fixture_ambiguous_identity) and the nine later scenarios, including both x20 parent-SIGKILL variants, did not run and are not PASS.

findings.detail: Probe.next lets the F1 'unresolved' event's deliberately changed anchor identity overwrite probe.supervisor, so unresolved_exit's fresh-identity check at line 2013 compares the live supervisor with a synthetic micros+1 identity and fails. Repair, limited to this test file: (1) In Probe.next, bind self.supervisor from the authoritative READY row (and keep it through terminal/result). For any later row with a 'supervisor' field, require pid/pgid/sid/uid/ppid/seconds to match the bound identity. Do not overwrite the binding from the 'unresolved' event; store that reported anchor separately, e.g. self.reported_unresolved_supervisor, so original_owned_processes records the true launch identity. If no supervisor is bound yet, keep the existing behaviour. (2) In unresolved_exit, keep the line-2013 check against the real supervisor identity, and add a check that the reported unresolved anchor differs from it only in micros (proving the fault was injected). (3) Add a deterministic ProbeDiagnosticsTests/ControllerCleanupTests regression: feed READY then an 'unresolved' row with changed micros, and assert probe.supervisor and inventory() keep the real identity. Do not change the _git_containment.py fault injection, F1 retention, containment_probe_parent.py, cleanup deadlines (2s F1 / 6s controller), signal policy or any other assertion. Do not remove or relax the line-2013 check. Source/test bytes must change, and the runner must rerun related checks, both full suites and all fourteen native scenarios.
